reading.body:
Thomas Kean's AI record is legislative and financial, not infrastructural: ten AI bill actions and four AI-adjacent committee contributions, with no datacenter, power, or compute item anywhere in the eighteen events.

The pattern is steady engagement across the whole span, from cosponsoring the TAKE IT DOWN Act in January 2025 to sponsoring the AI Emergency Button Act in September 2026. The bills cluster around two themes: deepfakes and intimate-image harms, and oversight of advanced or exportable AI. The money is narrower still. Three of the four contributions are $2,000 from Google's committee, spread across March, June, and July 2025 and July 2026, with a single $1,000 from Amazon's committee in June 2025.

For AI specifically, this is the governance layer, not the build layer. Nothing here touches siting, interconnection, or load, so it says nothing about whether AI compute gets built or where. What it does show is that the same member is writing rules about what models may do and who may export them, which is the part of AI policy that shapes deployment rather than capacity.

The data does not establish that any contribution influenced any bill, and the page's own framing declines to claim it. It also does not cover committee assignments, floor speeches, or anything Kean may have done on AI outside these eighteen dated records. Two of the votes are procedural motions to suspend the rules, which limits what can be read into them.

summary: Every dated AI event this site holds for Thomas Kean: bills sponsored or cosponsored, recorded votes on AI bills, and money from AI company and AI-focused political committees, newest first. 18 events.
